prejit_note: Keys computed with tools/djkey.py read-only on spark-eight (python -I via stdin, nothing written). Each source key reproduced itself. The same one-line N edit applied to the target's two 128-row N768 configs gives 0e915d63 -> ec8c0dc5 and 4ea90a59 -> 8135464c, both live target-compact entries that DeepGEMM JIT-compiled itself. So both tile configs map N768 -> N576 one to one. Cubin shas of the same kernel.cu differ between nodes (5559d059: 84ecdc26 on spark-one, 5cc4cce7 on spark-eight), so cubin_sha256 is recorded per node after the first prejit and not used as a gate.

device_checks: device_test.py on a stopped node: spark-eight first (exit 0), then with --real-weights on every node (each rank holds different expert slices), BEFORE any timing arm. Exit 0 = every case bitwise identical (FC1 columns, padded pad columns +0, FC2 input bytes + packed scales, MoE output; M32 and 128-row paths; eager and CUDA-graph replay; random, hostile and real mtp.0-2 weights). On a node with r1-pdl installed, run it a second time with DSV41_GLUE_PDL=fp (device_test calls deep_gemm_utils.dsv41_fused_permute, which r1-pdl hooks) to qualify the g17+pdl pair at E=128.

install_order: r1-pdl (if used) -> r2-moefront (if used) -> r2-draftmoe. Our installer also accepts r2-moefront installed on top of ours, but r2-moefront's own installer (as of this fix) only strips '# r1-pdl' and refuses a file with our lines, so it must go first unless it also strips '# r2-draftmoe' (our edits are pure tagged insertions, so stripping is exact).
uninstall_order: LIFO: r2-draftmoe -> r2-moefront -> r1-pdl. Our uninstall strips only our tagged lines after verifying the file is our patch of an accepted base, so it is correct in any order. r1-pdl's uninstall refuses (sha check) while our lines are present, so FIFO cannot silently drop our edits.
